summary: IPv6 allows a packet to carry a Fragment Header without being split, which are called atomic fragments. Hosts typically send them after a Packet Too Big error advertises a small next-hop MTU. Some implementations treat them like normal fragments and may reassemble them with other queued fragments, which is risky. This document describes the problem and updates processing to avoid it.

eli5.summary: Sometimes a package gets a "may be in pieces" sticker even though it is whole. Some computers then wrongly mix it with other pieces. This fixes that.

questions: how should ipv6 handle atomic fragments
